blocks.text: that an oil is obtained from mastic, as from other kinds of resin (صمغ [ṣamgh] צמגים) (Ki tissa [=?] 76^{b}).

Tournefort [=Tournefort, Relation d'un voyage du Levant] (st. [=died] 1708. Tschirch [=Tschirch, Handbuch der Pharmakognosie] 1, 906) reported on the harvesting of mastic on the island of Chios (Scio).

Arabic مصطكى [muṣṭakā] is a loanword (Fraenkel [=Fraenkel, Die aramäischen Fremdwörter im Arabischen] 151); it also migrated further into Armenian (Hübschmann [=Hübschmann, Armenische Etymologie] 248. ZDMG. [=Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenländischen Gesellschaft] 51, 304) and into the European languages.

For Arabic: E. Wiedem. [=Wiedemann, Beiträge zur Geschichte der Naturwissenschaften] 56, 340. mastik (P. [=Post, Flora of Syria, Palestine and Sinai]) Vullers [=Vullers, Lexicon Persico-Latinum] 2, 51 = رَمَاسى [ramāsī]. מצטכי Abulw. [=Abulwalīd Ibn Janāḥ, Kitāb al-uṣūl] 302 Bacher [=Bacher, Sepher haschoraschim]. Sha [=Steinschneider, Heilmittelnamen der Araber] 1879, Syriac كيا [kiyā] 1756. Physicians: Sha a. O. [=at the place cited] Kašef [=Kachef er-rumūz, transl. Leclerc] = كيا [kiyā]. Abu Salt [=Abū ṣ-Ṣalt, treatise on simple drugs]: משטיגי. Estori ha-Farḥī [=Estori ha-Farḥi, Kaftor waferaḥ] writes מצטכא and, in the name of his father, identifies it with קטף (f [=folio] 421^{b} Ven. [=Venice edition 1549], 107^{b} Edelm. [=ed. Edelmann, Berlin 1852], p. [=page] 662 Luncz [=ed. Luncz, Jerusalem 1899]).
Mastic is adulterated with the resin of the ʾubhul (juniper): Ibn Bassām [=Ibn Bassām, on ḥisba] in E. Wiedem. 40, 177. 189.

Romance forms among Jews: משתיק (Abulw. 302 Bacher), מסתיקי, מסתיצי Mb. [=?] 31. 50. Menaḥem b. Salomo [=Menaḥem ben Salomo, author of Sechel tob] (1139) says: lōṭ is the resin of the tree שטינקי (lentisco). In it. [=Italian] it is called משטיכו; it is a remedy and serves to strengthen the teeth (Sechel tob [=Menaḥem ben Salomo, Sechel tob, ed. Buber] p. 11). — Grünbaum, Jüd.-span. Chrest. [=Grünbaum, Jüdisch-spanische Chrestomathie] 11 f. [=and the following]: almastig, almaciga משטיק (Semag [=Sefer Mitzwot Gadol] lāwīn 65 f. 22^{a}). On account of the benedictions due to its fragrance, Tur [=Arbaʿa Ṭurim] and SchA [=Shulḥan ʿArukh] OCh. [=Oraḥ Ḥayyim] 216, 3 mention it — in the codices as מצטכי, in Zēdā lederech [=Ṣēdā la-derekh] 64^{b} as מצתכין, מצטיכי, מסטיכי.

Ever since Luther [=Martin Luther, German Bible translation] had rendered צרי*) in Ez. [=Ezekiel] 27, 17 by mastic, this was frequently repeated and is still retained by Rothstein [=Rothstein, translation of Ezekiel in Kautzsch] in the Kautzsch Bible (on ^{c d e}) and by others. ṣŏrī is not mastic but storax (Flora [=Löw, Die Flora der Juden] 3, 390), as Raši [=Rashi] on ^{a}) quite correctly states. In accordance with our usage one translates balsam (Rothstein), just as Abulwalīd [=Abulwalīd ibn Ğanāḥ, Book of Hebrew Roots] paraphrastically gives „tirjāḳ“, and as does the Geonic explanation in Ibn Esra [=Abraham Ibn Ezra], which understands by it a remedy compounded of 75 ingredients — that is, a theriac.

When Targ. j [=Targum Jerushalmi (Pseudo-Jonathan)] puts שרף (ו)קטף for it, it will mean storax. In any case Onkelos [=Targum Onkelos] with שעיף, samar. [=Samaritan (Targum)] שעבה (LAA. [=variant readings] שעפה, שעבי, שאבה) means not mastic but probably storax, not „balsam“ in general. In Palestine in the Talmudic period (3rd–4th Jh. [=century]) one sought

^{a} Gn. [=Genesis] 37, 25. ^{b} 43, 11. ^{c} Jer. [=Jeremiah] 8, 22. ^{d} 46, 11. ^{e} 51, 8. The Syrians and Greeks read צרי חיים in Sir. [=Sirach] 6, 16, but the LA. [=variant reading] of the Hebrew text, צרור חיים, is to be recognized as correct. — Susanna and Daniel 54–58 p. 138 Kautzsch [=Kautzsch, Die Apokryphen und Pseudepigraphen des Alten Testaments] does not belong here. — Boch. Hieroz. [=Bochart, Hierozoicon] 1, 628 wanted to derive ῥητίνη [rhētinē] from ṣŏrī. Wrong is the combination of Roubinovitch, ḥiddūšīm [=?] 6, that bh. [=Biblical Hebrew] עזק means the same as צרי.
